rule: A constraint may move in VOLLEY-lab without changing the controlled BOLLEY baseline. Physics, safety, evidence provenance and external requirements are not relaxed by calling a branch unbound.

assumptions.assumption: 3U remains the controlled payload class, with 4 kg reference and 6 kg qualification masses.
assumptions.reason: Keeps the selected baseline tied to a declared spacecraft class and mass envelope.
assumptions.current_cost: Constrains interface geometry, side-panel area, pressure area and CG envelope; no isolated mass cost exists.

attack.delete: Allow a purpose-built non-3U bus in an Unbound branch.
attack.move: Put compatibility in a removable Fluxsleeve or launcher-owned carrier.
attack.invert: Choose spacecraft geometry around the deployment machine instead of fitting the machine around 3U.
attack.merge: Use the spacecraft primary frame as the deployment interface.
attack.scale: Screen other form factors only after a mission case defines why.

assumptions.assumption: The controlled reference shot reaches 11.8 m/s within 0.90 m and no more than 8 g.
assumptions.reason: Defines the current mechanical duty and preserves the corrected A10 consistency.
assumptions.current_cost: Sets force and powered length; separate installed cost is incomplete.

attack.delete: Let the host create most relative velocity through burn-and-drop.
attack.move: Split bulk acceleration and precision trim between mechanisms.
attack.invert: Choose available host stroke first, then compute reachable release velocity.
attack.merge: Use a stage structural member as the powered guide.
attack.scale: Search longer low-acceleration and shorter high-acceleration strokes without changing the controlled requirement.

assumptions.assumption: Exit tip-off is limited to 2 deg/s per axis.
assumptions.reason: Protects separation quality and follows the tighter flown dispenser class used by VOLLEY.
assumptions.current_cost: Drives CG knowledge, four-channel allocation, end-effect control and 6-DOF work.

attack.delete: Only if a named payload and provider accept another limit.
attack.move: Use spacecraft attitude control to pre-bias or damp rate before release.
attack.invert: Command a deliberate release rate if the mission values it.
attack.merge: Use pressure quadrants or trim channels for both centring and tip-off correction.
attack.scale: Map reachable translational and rotational release states.

assumptions.assumption: The cooperative interface should add no more than 0.25 kg and shall add no more than 0.40 kg.
assumptions.reason: Stops the spacecraft concession from becoming hidden launcher mass.
assumptions.current_cost: The selected 0.37136 kg interface misses the preference by 0.12136 kg.

attack.delete: Remove gross interface mass as an objective only in a branch that closes full spacecraft system mass.
attack.move: Move special material to a removable launcher-owned sleeve.
attack.invert: Require the interface to replace more spacecraft mass than it adds.
attack.merge: Combine structure, thermal spreading, grounding, guidance and deployment functions.
attack.scale: Search net added mass against real bus architectures.

assumptions.assumption: Spacecraft-side deployment hardware is passive and carries no powered coils, permanent magnets, pressure vessels, pyrotechnics or launch-time software.
assumptions.reason: Keeps integration burden below adding a spacecraft propulsion system.
assumptions.current_cost: Forces active field generation, sensing and stored energy onto the launcher; P41 questions that retained pulse.

attack.delete: Allow powered spacecraft-side deployment hardware in a dedicated lab branch.
attack.move: Move only sensing or switching onto the spacecraft while energy remains launcher-side.
attack.invert: Let the spacecraft command final trim or centring.
attack.merge: Reuse active deployment hardware as attitude, structural sensing, thermal or docking hardware after release.
attack.scale: Bound active spacecraft mass and power from sensing to local trim actuation.

assumptions.assumption: The external sliding/contact surface remains hard-anodized aluminium and retains applicable provider rail geometry.
assumptions.reason: Preserves a credible contact surface until a provider-specific interface replaces preliminary CDS guidance.
assumptions.current_cost: Adds magnetic gap and constrains stator access, contact area and side-panel use; P3, P19 and P20 remain open.

attack.delete: Use a purpose-built spacecraft or provider interface in Unbound work.
attack.move: Put wear/contact geometry on a removable sleeve.
attack.invert: Design the guide around the electromagnetic/pressure interface rather than preserving a legacy rail first.
attack.merge: Make the guide part of the pressure seal land or thermal/structural frame.
attack.scale: Compare rail, broad-face, corner-land and collar interfaces on one provider boundary.

assumptions.assumption: The controlled electromagnetic shot is capped at 900 J gross stored-energy draw and 15 kW preferred peak launcher power.
assumptions.reason: Prevents BOLLEY from recreating VOLLEY's pulse-power problem under another geometry.
assumptions.current_cost: A7c leaves 6.588 J of model energy margin; P11, P39, P40 and P41 remain controlling.

attack.delete: Delete the shot-time pulse with gas, mechanical storage or host propulsion.
attack.move: Pre-store energy mechanically or pneumatically close to the actuator.
attack.invert: Use electromagnetics only for low-energy trim after bulk acceleration.
attack.merge: Share source, structure or thermal hardware only where a complete mass ledger supports the credit.
attack.scale: Search the boundary between bulk impulse and precision trim rather than only lowering electrical loss.

assumptions.assumption: No launcher propulsion member requires capture after release.
assumptions.reason: Deletes the sled brake, return stroke and post-release moving launcher member that motivated BOLLEY.
assumptions.current_cost: Pushes the special moving interface onto the spacecraft and constrains fallback architectures.

attack.delete: Permit a launcher-owned carrier only if full capture/arrest/return mass beats the controlled interface cost.
attack.move: Let a removable sleeve depart with the payload.
attack.invert: Treat a launcher-owned carrier as compatibility mode and direct interface as native mode.
attack.merge: Make any departing carrier remain useful as spacecraft structure.
attack.scale: Search short trim shuttles separately from full-stroke movers.

assumptions.assumption: An independent fail-safe retention gate carries ascent loads and inhibits firing.
assumptions.current_cost: Adds a mechanism, structural load path and fault tree that remain unsized.

attack.delete: Only if a provider-approved retention architecture replaces it.
attack.move: Integrate retention into the host dispenser or spacecraft structure.
attack.invert: Use propulsion geometry to remain locked until a separate safe condition releases it.
attack.merge: Combine retention, inhibit and position sensing only where failure independence is preserved.
attack.scale: Compare one central gate, four face locks and provider-native retention.

assumptions.lab_route: none until a concrete mechanism exists

assumptions.assumption: Commanded exit-velocity dispersion is initially no more than 0.10 m/s at 3 sigma.
assumptions.reason: Defines the precision claim behind programmable deployment.
assumptions.current_cost: Requires sensing, repeatability, force calibration and precision authority.

attack.delete: Only if orbital work shows the mission does not value that precision.
attack.move: Allow coarse bulk acceleration and precise final trim.
attack.invert: Command a reachable distribution rather than one target velocity if mission utility supports it.
attack.merge: Use the same estimator for CG, position and exit-state correction.
attack.scale: Map mission value versus dispersion instead of treating 0.10 m/s as universally optimal.

assumptions.assumption: The unpowered cooperative interface adds no more than 50 microtesla above ambient outside the static payload envelope.
assumptions.reason: Protects magnetometers and attitude sensors from a permanent spacecraft-side disturbance.
assumptions.current_cost: Restricts material state and discourages permanent magnets; hardware measurement is absent.

attack.delete: Only for a named bus whose sensor architecture tolerates another field.
attack.move: Place magnetic material on a removable launcher-owned element.
attack.invert: Actively cancel or calibrate the field if spacecraft participation is allowed.
attack.merge: Use magnetic hardware for another orbital function only if the system architecture closes.
attack.scale: Map field versus sensor distance and bus layout.

assumptions.assumption: Four face channels provide independent force allocation across the declared transverse CG envelope.
assumptions.reason: Moves the commanded force centroid toward the actual payload CG.
assumptions.current_cost: Multiplies stator channels, sensing, calibration and fault cases.

attack.delete: Use fewer channels only if 6-DOF analysis closes tip-off on the same CG envelope.
attack.move: Put part of the authority into pressure quadrants or spacecraft attitude control.
attack.invert: Use channel imbalance deliberately for lateral or rotational release commands.
attack.merge: Use the same channels for axial force, centring and final trim.
attack.scale: Search two, three, four and distributed-channel architectures.

assumptions.assumption: Every externally retained part remains attached through ascent, deployment and mission operation.
assumptions.reason: Prevents debris and uncontrolled released hardware.
assumptions.current_cost: Forces capture, encapsulation and load paths into every cooperative interface.

attack.move: Move sacrificial or wear parts onto provider-approved launcher hardware.
attack.invert: Design intentionally departing hardware only if it becomes part of the spacecraft after separation.
attack.merge: Make covers and wear surfaces structural or thermal members.
attack.scale: Compare monolithic, bonded and mechanically captured constructions.

assumptions.assumption: Deployment is primarily axial and one payload is released at a time.
assumptions.reason: Keeps the controlled mechanism, collision geometry and force allocation tractable.
assumptions.current_cost: Leaves lateral release authority and recoil-cancelling paired release unexplored.

attack.delete: Allow vector and paired release in lab studies.
attack.move: Use host attitude or orbital timing for some separation dimensions.
attack.invert: Choose payload pairs and release vectors to minimise host impulse.
attack.merge: Use four-channel authority for centring and commanded lateral/rotational state.
attack.scale: Map the full six-dimensional reachable departure-state envelope.

assumptions.assumption: Nitrogen is the current Fluxpiston screening fluid.
assumptions.reason: Provides an inert reference fluid for the first gas-system screen.
assumptions.current_cost: Sets storage volume, thermal state, leakage mass flow and plume composition; no complete system optimum exists.

attack.delete: Remove a dedicated deployment fluid if the host supplies a suitable source.
attack.move: Use host pressurant or another stage fluid only with a named system boundary.
attack.invert: Choose the fluid from thermal, storage and contamination requirements before sizing the interface.
attack.merge: Share storage or regulation with a host subsystem only if provider evidence permits.
attack.scale: Compare fluids on stored-system mass, contamination and transient response.
